metadata.title: Your First Brutalist Project.
metadata.audience: Humanitarians AI fellows already using Claude Code
metadata.note: Portrait (9:16) companion of the landscape reel. Native 2160 x 3840 layouts — every beat uses a portrait-registered composition (Composer916, HesitantWriter916, CodeBeat916, VerdictArtifact916, TitleOutroHAI916). Not a crop. Narration text is authored short so the smaller portrait card can hold it. Code samples on B02 and B07 use tightly wrapped snippets that fit the narrower card. Same substance as the landscape master, laid out for a phone.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI, first-project ask, four-line plan. Portrait-native composer.
beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. Your first Brutalist project starts here. One ask into Claude Code, one plan back. Not a demo — a claim with a clock.

shot.show: portrait composer with the first-project ask and a four-line plan

props.command: claude "make me a 60-second AI Explainer about how ribosomes read mRNA — 12 beats, Kokoro am_onyx"

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer. Correction: demo -> claim.
beats.narration_text: So here's the frame. Your first project is not a demo of a tool. It's a claim — a small research question, with evidence — that Claude Code renders into a one minute film you can rebuild, beat by beat. That is the whole method.

shot.show: portrait hesitant writer types the frame and corrects demo -> claim

beats.role_note: framework — what a beat sheet IS. Portrait code card with tight lines.
beats.narration_text: The video is a file. beat_sheet dot json holds every beat, its narration, its visual pattern, and its measured audio length. Change a line here — you re-render one beat, not a whole reel.

shot.show: portrait code card — a single beat as it lives on disk

beats.role_note: ASK-RESULT pair 1 — concrete first ask, portrait composer.
beats.narration_text: Here is a first ask, verbatim. A specific topic, a length, the beat count, the voice, and a hard stop at the review cut so nothing final gets built before you have watched it.

shot.show: portrait composer with the specific first-project ask

props.command: claude "use ai-explainer to make a 60s reel on how ribosomes read mRNA. 12 beats, am_onyx, review cut only."

beats.role_note: the seven concrete steps the pipeline touches. Portrait artifact card.
beats.narration_text: Claude Code does seven concrete things before you see a frame. It reads the skill, drafts the beat sheet, generates the audio, renders the scenes, compiles the review cut, writes the checks report, and stops. Every one leaves a file you can open.

shot.show: portrait artifact card with the seven concrete pipeline steps

artifactLines: reads skills/make/ai-explainer/SKILL.md
drafts beat_sheet.json (twelve beats)
generates mp3/beat-*.mp3 (Kokoro am_onyx)
renders media/*.mp4 (Remotion, per beat)
compiles clips/ -> review-cut.mp4 at 4K
writes CHECKS-REPORT.md and _qc/ frames
stops for you to watch, before anything final

beats.role_note: review cut is a receipt, not publication.
beats.narration_text: The output is a review cut. Twelve conformed clips, one narration per beat, four thousand pixels wide. That's the file you scrub. Not a Short. Not a published master. A local receipt that says: the pipeline finished — now you judge it.

shot.show: portrait artifact card — the review cut receipt

props.artifactHeading: The pipeline finished. Now you judge it.
artifactLines: twelve conformed per-beat clips in clips/
muxed to one review-cut.mp4 at 3840 x 2160
narration is the master clock — visuals conform
a per-beat manifest hashes each input for cache
not a Short, not a published master, a receipt
human review is a separate step — you watch it

beats.narration_text: Something is off. Beat five drags. So you don't rebuild the film. You say what's wrong, and name the beat. Claude regenerates only that beat's audio, re-renders only that beat's scene, and re-muxes. Everything else is cached.

shot.show: portrait composer with the revision ask

props.command: claude "beat five is too long. cut to twenty words, regenerate audio, re-render only that scene, rebuild the review cut."

beats.role_note: the tiny on-disk change after a one-beat revision. Portrait code diff card.
beats.narration_text: The diff on disk is small: one mp3 replaced, one mp4 replaced, one line in the beat sheet. That's why audio is the clock and every beat is a slot. You change a beat by changing its slot — not by nudging a timeline.

shot.show: portrait code card — the diff from a one-beat revision

props.title: diff — one-beat revision
props.code:
M  beat_sheet.json
   # narration_text on B05
M  mp3/beat-B05.mp3
   # Kokoro am_onyx
M  media/B05.mp4
   # Remotion re-render
M  clips/B05.mp4
   # compile.py conform
M  review-cut.mp4
   # concat + mux only

# 5 files changed.
# 11 clips cached.
# Audio is the clock.
# A beat is a slot.

beats.role_note: format discipline — 9:16 is a separate sheet, not a crop.
beats.narration_text: Now the shape of the deliverable. Fellows owe two ratios per video, sixteen by nine and nine by sixteen. The vertical is not a crop of the landscape. It is its own beat sheet, in a sibling folder, with portrait-native scenes. The art vertical skill plans that sheet — you still author it.

props.artifactHeading: 9:16 is a separate sheet, never a crop.
artifactLines: landscape master: 3840 x 2160
portrait: 2160 x 3840 (this file)
art vertical PLANS a portrait sheet
you still author each portrait beat
portrait-native scenes (Composer916, Outro916)
compile.py renders each at 4K
no cropping, no upscaling

beats.role_note: runtime receipt is not publication approval.
beats.narration_text: And the handoff. Source goes to GitHub — the beat sheet, prompts, checks, README, anything under twenty-five megabytes. Video files go to Drive. A compile that finishes is a runtime receipt. It is not publication approval. That's the human review step, and it comes last.

shot.show: portrait artifact — source vs. video destinations

props.artifactHeading: Source to GitHub. Video to Drive.
artifactLines: beat_sheet.json, README, PROMPTS.md -> GitHub
MP4s and MP3s -> Google Drive folder
over-25-MB files always to Drive, not repo
no credentials or private data anywhere
'compile finished' is a runtime receipt
human review is a separate step
publishing happens later — outside this pipeline

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — greeting Your Turn, paste-ready prompt, good/bad ask discussion.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this prompt into Claude Code in a fresh folder, and swap in your topic. A good first ask names one small question, states the length in seconds, and stops at the review cut. A bad first ask says 'make me a video' and hopes.

shot.show: portrait composer with the paste-ready first-project prompt

props.command: claude "use skills/make/ai-explainer to make a 60s Brutalist AI Explainer about [my tiny question]. 12 beats, am_onyx, stop at the review cut."
output: GOOD: one question, length, hard stop
BAD: 'make me a video' with no shape
watch the review cut — request ONE revision
